quests.title: Central Park pest control
quests.text: Leomon cannot leave the gym, and Kunemon keep wandering into Central Park. Thin them out.

offer.name: Leomon
lines: Hey there. The Kunemon have been wandering into Central Park again, and I cannot leave the gym to deal with them.
If you could thin out three of them, I would be grateful. I will make it worth your while.
Can you do that?
doneLines: Three less to worry about. Thank you.
Take this, you earned it.

Will you do that?
doneLines: So the road holds. That is a weight off my mind.
Here, for your trouble.

quests.title: East Station bounty: forest greens
quests.text: Plants are overrunning the Kicking Forest path. Cut four of them back.

quests.title: South Station bounty: swamp pests
quests.text: The Bulk Swamp crossing is infested. Clear four of the worst offenders.

quests.title: The quiet route
quests.text: Couriers lose time to fights in the Wire Forest. Show a fight-free way through.

objectives.label: Cross the Wire Forest entrance from the north-west gate to the south gate without a fight

quests.title: Card ladder: first steps
quests.text: Prove yourself at the card table. Beat any three tamers.

quests.title: Card ladder: rising duelist
quests.text: Word is spreading. Beat six tamers in all.

quests.title: Double trouble in Central Park
quests.text: Two pests came out of the long grass at once. Face a Kunemon and a Tapirmon back to back, with no time to heal in between.

objectives.label: Beat a Kunemon and then a Tapirmon, back to back

offer.name: Leomon
lines: Something odd happened. Two pests came out of the long grass at the same time, a Kunemon and a Tapirmon.
Could you face them back to back? No time to heal in between. It is harder than it sounds.
Will you try?
doneLines: Both of them at once, and you are still standing. Impressive.
Here you go.
remindLines: Still after those two? A Kunemon, then a Tapirmon, back to back.
Do not stop to rest in between. Good luck.

quests.title: Seiryu's rematch
quests.text: Word is the Seiryu leader's team will take on all comers again. The same three fighters, in the same order.

objectives.label: Beat the three fighters in a row

quests.title: Seiryu's rematch: the hard way
quests.text: The same three fighters, but they have been training. Stronger and tougher.

objectives.label: Beat the three trained fighters in a row

quests.title: Three leaders, one afternoon
quests.text: Take on the Seiryu, Suzaku and Byakko teams one after another. No healing between rounds.

objectives.label: Beat all three leaders' teams in a row (eight fights)

quests.title: Circuit Board cartographer
quests.text: The underground Circuit Board boards are not on any map. Chart six different ones.

objectives.label: Chart different Circuit Board boards

quests.title: Before and after
quests.text: The Main Lobby is not always the same place. See it as it is now, and again once the city has changed.

objectives.label: Visit the Main Lobby once as Asuka City and once as Amaterasu City

quests.title: Arena qualifiers
quests.text: Three qualifier matches, back to back, on the arena floor. The game's own tournament rounds were never filled in; these are new.

objectives.label: Win three qualifier matches in a row on the arena floor

quests.title: Guilmon cannot find his tamer
quests.text: Your Guilmon keeps looking past you for a tamer who is not there. Follow the trail and bring them together.

objectives.name: Agumon
lines: Guilmon is looking for his tamer? He is not in the station.
I saw a tamer with a very familiar hat heading for Qing Long City. Try there.

objectives.name: Takato
lines: Guilmon? Is that you? I looked everywhere!
I am sorry I kept you waiting. Thank you for bringing him to me.

lines: You have beaten a lot of Kunemon by now. Did you notice how they move?
A partner that knows an enemy that well can take on its shape.
Fight on. Around level fourteen, your partner should learn the Kunemon form.
Will you try?
doneLines: I saw it in the way your partner stood. That is the Kunemon form.
It is not a real Digivolution, but it is yours. Here, take this.
remindLines: Still no Kunemon form? Keep fighting. Around level fourteen it should come to your partner.
It arrives after a victory, so do not stop now.

quests.title: Beginner's luck
quests.text: The Girl bet her lunch that she could teach a stranger to duel in one afternoon. Win a card duel so she eats.

offer.name: Girl
lines: Hey! You! You have cards, right? Everybody has cards. Nobody has good cards, but everybody has cards!
I bet my lunch I could turn a total beginner into a duelist today. You look like a total beginner.
Win one duel, any duel, and I eat. Lose, and I swap lunches with my Digimon. Please?
doneLines: You won! I mean, I knew you would. I told everybody. Nobody was listening, but I told them.
Lunch is saved. Here, take this, and don't tell my Digimon I shared.
remindLines: One duel! Even a bad one counts. Even a really, really lucky one.
My stomach is already writing you a letter.

remindLines: Level ten. That is the number. Everything below is a rounding error.

quests.title: A complete set of disks
quests.text: The Gentleman collects one of each ordinary healing disk. Bring him an Antidote, a Sober, an Energy and a Revive Disk.

offer.name: Gentleman
lines: Good day. I collect disks. Healing disks, to be precise. One of each kind, set neatly on a velvet cloth.

lines: I have crossed deserts. I have crossed seas. I have not crossed this forest, because of those Flymon.
Two of them, buzzing at the entrance, and they will not let me past. I would fight, but I am a traveler, not a fighter.
Clear two and I will tell you a good story. Maybe two.
doneLines: The road is clear! And just in time. I was starting to repeat a story about a goat.
Here. And I will tell you about the goat sometime. Not now.
remindLines: Two Flymon at the entrance. Then I can finally cross.
I have been here three days. The stories are getting repetitive.

Take this. It keeps the wind off. Next time, I will not go easy.

I will not rush you. The gym has stood a long time. It will stand a little longer.

doneLines: Excellent! Notice the difference in the shell texture? No? Neither do I, but the clipboard does.
Your payment, and a promise to thank you in the footnote. Everyone gets a footnote.

They notice the clipboard. Do not ask me how.

Start at the entrance and walk to the west forest. Report back.
doneLines: Teeth buzzing, and a faint hum, and a feeling of being watched by a tree? Marvellous. Data!
A little reward, and a promise to credit you. Under Feelings.
remindLines: Wire Forest entrance, then the west forest. Does anything hum? Do your teeth buzz?

Here is a bit of money. And I will name a very small beetle after you.

objectives.label: Visit Shell Beach and Plug Cape

offer.name: Traveler
lines: About that goat. I owe you a story. The trouble is I have forgotten the middle, and the end.
It happened somewhere on a coast. If you go to Shell Beach and Plug Cape, one of them might remind me. Bring me a detail from each.
A smell. A sound. Whatever you remember. Then I will tell it properly.
doneLines: A bell! A BELL! Of course. The goat rang it to scare the tide. Now I remember the whole thing.
Here is a little something for the story. The goat sends its regards, if goats could.

Four of them, thrashing about, and every fish within a mile is hiding. Quieter water, better bite.
I do not mind waiting. But I would like to wait with a bite.
doneLines: The water is quiet. A fish nibbled just now. It was polite about it.
Take this. The sea gave it to me, and I am giving it to you. That is how the sea works.

I am in no hurry. But the tide is.

Fight it, if you must. Gently, if you can. And tell me what it said.
doneLines: So it was a Shellmon, and it was only sleepy. That explains the tide.
Here is your pay, and my thanks. The sea sends hers too.
remindLines: The big shell off Plug Cape. It moves. It listens. It has opinions.

doneLines: Someone saw it! Not sails, a very big cloud shaped like sails. But it counts!
Here. A lookout always pays his scouts. It is in the manual. I am writing the manual.

quests.text: Something has been wailing in the Tranquil Swamp for three nights and Ghostbuster Puck will not go near the water. Ask the old man at the Bulk Swamp what it is, then stand in the reeds and wait for it.

objectives.name: Old Man
lines: A wailing in the reeds. My father would have called it a guest with no inn.
I have heard it twice. It is not angry. Angry has a rhythm to it. This one is only sad, and sad is mostly cold.
Ghosts have no use for bedding. If it takes a warm thing from you and says thank you, it is not a ghost.

quests.text: The youngest Gatomon at the Swamp Inn has never been allowed to run a night alone. Find her one guest brave enough to stay, clear the Gekomon out of the cellar, and give the common room one good card duel.

Tell her I will pay, and tell her I do not snore, which is a lie she will find out about.

offer.name: Tailmon
lines: You. Do you sleep? Not here. Nobody sleeps here any more.
I am a trainee manager. I have made eleven beds, folded four hundred towels, and never run one night on my own. Tonight the others are in the city and the desk is mine.
A manager needs a guest. Find me one. And the cellar has a Gekomon in it that sings all night, and a guest who cannot sleep does not come back.
And this inn has a card table in the common room and nobody has ever played one game at it. One duel. That is all a good night needs.
doneLines: He stayed. He actually stayed. He is asleep in room two with the lamp on.
And the cellar is quiet, and there are cards on the table with the corner turned up. I ran one night. I did a whole night.
Here. This is from the inn, not from me, so you cannot refuse it. Come back and sleep in a bed like a person.
remindLines: A guest. Anyone with legs and a blanket. The one in the swamp who is scared of ghosts never sleeps anyway.
And the cellar. A Gekomon. It is not dangerous, it is only loud, and loud is the enemy of a good inn.
And one card duel at my table. I want somebody to lean on the desk and watch, the way guests do.

quests.title: A Cap of Her Own
quests.text: The girl who follows Tamer Andy everywhere has never won a fight of her own. Beat the pair that blocks the station road at night and win one card duel, so she can watch from close up how it is done.

objectives.label: Beat the pair that blocks the station road

offer.name: Girl
lines: You are a tamer. A real one. I have seen the way you walk.
I am Andy's groupie. I have followed him since the East. I know his favourite disk, his lucky folder, and the way he says yah when he is losing.
I have never won anything. Not one duel, not one fight. I want to watch a real one from very close before I try it, and nobody duels a groupie.
So. Beat the Triceramon and the Tuskmon that block the station road at night. Then win one card duel. I will stand near enough to see how a winner stands.
doneLines: You did it. You did it the way I thought it was done.
Except you made a mistake in the second round and you laughed at it. Andy never laughs when he loses. He says yah.
I have been practising being him for a year. I think I would rather practise being me for a while. Ask me something.
remindLines: The station road at night. A Triceramon and a Tuskmon. They are not clever, they are just wide.
And one duel. Any table. I will watch your hands, not your cards.
offer.ask: Show me how it is done?

Tell him? No. He would say something kind and I would go back to following him.
I will stand at the station for a while and see if I still like the wind. That is enough of a plan.
Take this. A school cap. I will need a new one anyway, one that is not a costume.

objectives.label: Follow the little prints into the cave

offer.name: Boy
lines: Hey! Hey. You. You are a real tamer, right? With a badge and everything. Good. I need a deputy.
I am the night watch of Byakko City. I made myself the night watch because nobody else would. Something keeps taking the flower pots off the wall. One every night.
I keep falling asleep at the important part. So: deputy. First we duel, because that is the rule, and I wrote the rule.
doneLines: All six! In a nest! You found the whole crime scene and the crime scene is a nest.
Wait. Wait wait wait. That is a Numemon nest. Numemon. The one who got everybody out of that cave. That Numemon.
I need to sit down. The watch is sitting down for a minute.
remindLines: The duel first. A deputy who has not duelled is just a person standing next to me.
Then the little prints. They go down. Down is the cave under the city. I am not going down there. The watch stays up. That is the whole point of a watch.

The wind. Right. The wind took six flower pots off a wall and put them in a nest.

He has been standing behind the seats talking to a wall. I heard a bit of it. He is practising asking someone to dinner at the oasis.
Do not tell him I told you. He will make me do drills, and I am a student, not a soldier.

Everybody else has given me a line and every line is about themselves. His is the longest and it has the word I in it nine times.
Get his notes. If they are his, I will write his line and that is that. If they are not his, I still need a line, and I would rather have yours.

quests.title: The guest who never left
quests.text: Tailmon has a room paid for a week by a guest nobody has seen. Look in the Underground Cave and the Secret Room for a trace.

offer.name: Tailmon
lines: There is a room upstairs paid for a week. Paid! And in all that time I have not seen one hair of the guest.
I do not like it. A guest who pays and does not appear is either very shy or up to something.
Walk the Underground Cave and the Secret Room and see if a stranger is sleeping rough there. Will you?
doneLines: Little muddy prints by the cave mouth. So the guest is real, and the guest is messy.
Here, for the walk. I am keeping the room. Something tells me to keep the room.

offer.ask: Go and look for the guest?

objectives.name: Office Lady
lines: A room paid but never used? I know the one. Interesting handwriting. Very small letters.
Whoever wrote it ordered two breakfasts, every day. Two. Nobody orders two unless they are afraid to eat alone.

lines: A thing that walks at night and leaves little prints? Dear, half this city does.

The Office Lady reads handwriting like a fortune teller. The Old Woman reads nights like a book.
Ask them both, in that order, and bring me what they say. Will you?
doneLines: Two breakfasts and crumbs. So the guest is small, hungry and afraid of the dark.
I have stopped being annoyed and started feeling sorry. Bring me a name, please.
remindLines: The Office Lady first, then the Old Woman. Two breakfasts is the clue.
The kitchen is still making two and I am still pretending not to mind.

quests.title: The face in the fog
quests.text: Something in Byakko City is wearing the missing guest's face. Win a fight against it before it wears yours.

objectives.label: Win a fight against the shape wearing the guest's face

offer.name: Tailmon
lines: I saw it on the stairs. It had the guest's little prints and no face at all, and then it had my face.
It is not a guest. It is something that puts guests on like a coat.
I am an innkeeper, not a hero. Will you deal with it before it wears the whole city?
doneLines: You broke the coat. Under it was a small, frightened, very smelly shape, and it ran upstairs.
Straight into the paid room. I knew that room was wrong. I did not know it was a nest.
remindLines: It is still on the stairs at night. It waved at me with my own hand.
Please. It is copying my best coat now.

quests.title: The smallest guest
quests.text: The guest is a frightened Numemon hiding in the paid room. Learn the Numemon form so it has a friendly face to answer.

offer.name: Tailmon
lines: It is a Numemon. Small, shy, and it paid for a whole week so it would not have to move.
It ordered two breakfasts because it was too scared to eat in the dining room and took one up.
If your partner learned the Numemon shape, it might open the door. Can you try?
doneLines: It opened the door! It shook my hand, and your partner's, and then it cried a bit.
Here, take these. The smallest guest paid me in buttons and I am passing the best on to you.
remindLines: The smallest guest is still in room nine. It eats the second breakfast at midnight.
A friendly face is the only key I do not have.

quests.title: A secret cheaper than lunch
quests.text: The Black Hat will trade a Badland secret for a cleared road. Thin out the Etemon squatting on it.

offer.name: Black Hat
lines: Psst. Over here. Do not look like you are buying anything.
I have a secret about this Badland. Cheap. Practically free. But free always has a price.
Two Etemon are sitting on the road I need and I do not fight. Move them and the secret is yours. Dealing?

Here, take this before I become unbearable.

Go and stand in it and tell me if it is stranger than I am. Will you?
doneLines: Stranger than you and stranger than me. That is a high bar and it cleared it.
Here. Now I have been lost in the idea of two deserts and that will do.
remindLines: The south Noise Desert. Strange in a way nobody will describe.
If it is stranger than me, be gentle when you say so.

quests.title: A look at the works
quests.text: Wizardmon wants to know what the Dum Dum Factory actually makes. Get close enough to have an opinion.

offer.name: Wizardmon
lines: A practical question for a change. The Dum Dum Factory. What does it make?
Nobody I ask knows, and the name suggests it makes Dum Dums, which cannot be a real product.
Go and look until you have an opinion. Any opinion. Will you?
doneLines: Noise. It makes noise and parts and more noise. An opinion at last.
Here. You have solved a riddle nobody was asking and I am delighted.
remindLines: The Dum Dum Factory. Look at it until it means something.
If it makes Dum Dums, buy two. I want to see one.

quests.title: Disks for the inn
quests.text: Tailmon keeps her guests comfortable and is low on Antidote Disks. Bring her three.

offer.name: Tailmon
lines: An inn is only as good as its sick tray. My sick tray is empty and my guests are sneezing.
Three Antidote Disks and I can face the morning rush with a clear conscience.
Bring three and I will overpay, which I hate. Will you?
doneLines: The tray is full. My conscience is clear and my wallet is annoyed.
Here. And a favour, which is not the same as overpaying. It is cheaper.
remindLines: Three Antidote Disks for the sick tray. The sneezing is getting competitive.
I am overpaying. Do not tell the other guests.

quests.title: Fuel for the range
quests.text: Gargomon tests gear all day and runs on Energy Disks. Bring him two and he will call it a fair trade.

offer.name: Gargomon
lines: BANG! Sorry. Testing. I test all day and I run on Energy Disks and I am empty.
Two of them. Crunchy ones. They keep the hands steady and the hands are everything.
Bring two and I will pay and shout in a friendly way. Will you?
doneLines: CRUNCH. Good. Steady hands. Excellent. You have saved a whole afternoon of testing.
Here. The pay. BANG. That one was a test.
remindLines: Two Energy Disks! BANG. Sorry. Two.
My hands are wobbling and a wobbly hand is a wasted test.

quests.title: A sober collection
quests.text: The Gentleman collects Sober Disks and is three short of a neat row. Bring him three.

offer.name: Gentleman
lines: I collect Sober Disks. Not for use. For the row. The row must end in a whole number.
I am three short and the row looks, to my eye, deeply unsettled.
Bring three and restore order to my shelf. Will you?
doneLines: The row is complete. It is magnificent. It is a row.
Here, a rarer disk for you, so that you too may start a row.
remindLines: Three Sober Disks. The row is three short and it is all I can see.
A row is a promise you make to yourself, in circles.

Two Revive Disks. I will carry them and never use them, which is how I like my supplies.
Bring two. I pay in full and speak in short sentences. Will you?
doneLines: Two. Good. I will carry them and think of you, briefly, which is a lot for me.
Take this. It is not sentiment. It is payment. Mostly.
remindLines: Two Revive Disks. For the road. Unused, ideally.
A spare is a promise to yourself. I keep my promises.

quests.text: The Old Woman in the cave is tired and asks for one Life Disk, which she will pretend is for someone else.

offer.name: Old Woman
lines: Dear, fetch me one Life Disk. It is not for me, of course. It is for a friend.
The friend is also me. We have discussed it and agreed to lie to you.
One disk and I will sit up straight for a whole afternoon. Will you?
doneLines: Ah. There. The friend feels better, and so do I, and we are both me.
Here. Take this. A small thank you from a small conspiracy.
remindLines: One Life Disk for my friend, who is me. She is waiting patiently.
Do not tell the Old Man. He will make it a riddle.

I want three. Not for a fight. Just to be sure about the taste.
Will you bring three? I will pay and I will share one, possibly.
doneLines: THUNDER. It is thunder. You have to try one. No, that was the last one. Sorry.
Here is the pay. And this. I found it and I did not eat it. Progress.

If I share one it will be a small one. I am being honest up front.

Do not ask what the experiment is. Asking is how experiments become accidents.
Bring two Super Charges and I will reward you with a stronger reagent. Will you?
doneLines: Both hum. The experiment proceeds and the mat is honoured.
Here is a stronger reagent for you. Do not ask what it is. You already know the rule.
remindLines: Two Super Charges. The experiment is patient and slightly dangerous.
I have set out a small mat for the reagents. They like a mat.

quests.text: The Schoolgirl read that Max Charges are the strongest thing a shop sells. She wants two to be sure.

lines: I read that Max Charges are the strongest thing you can buy. Strongest how? It does not say. Books are like that.
I want two. One to look at and one to look at later.
Will you bring two before I read something even more alarming?
doneLines: They are heavier than the book said. That is a finding. I have written it down as HEAVY.
Here. A thank you, and a promise to only read normal books for a week.
remindLines: Two Max Charges. Strongest thing, allegedly. My book is vague and my curiosity is not.
I have labelled a shelf. It says STRONG. Two of them would look right there.

Two Power Charges. They are candy if you are determined, and I am extremely determined.
Bring two and I will tell you the good rumour, not the ordinary one. Will you?
doneLines: Bless you. I can feel my opinions returning. Here is the good rumour. It has two names, not one.
And here is your payment, which is sweeter than the candy. Financially.
remindLines: Two Power Charges. The meeting is approaching like weather.
The good rumour has a name in it. Hurry.

lines: I sell gear. Good gear. I do not sell good gear to a partner that folds in a stiff breeze.
Level 26. Then we talk about the good shelf. The good shelf has a lock and I have the key.
Come back at 26 and the key turns. Will you?
doneLines: 26! The key turns. Look at the good shelf and try not to gasp. Everyone gasps.
Here, from the middle shelf. The top shelf is for 30 and up.
remindLines: Level 26. The good shelf is dusty and patient.
I am not being rude. A locked shelf is a compliment waiting to happen.

quests.title: A guest worth bragging about
quests.text: Tailmon only brags about guests whose partners reach level 30. Reach it and she will brag.

offer.name: Tailmon
lines: I brag about my guests. It is my one indulgence and I am excellent at it.
I cannot brag about you yet. You are level something, and something is not a brag.
Reach 30 and I will brag to the whole hall. Will you?
doneLines: THIRTY. Everyone, listen. This one reached thirty. I said so. It is true. Bragging is easy when it is true.
Here, wear this while I find somebody else to tell.
remindLines: Level 30. Then the bragging. I have been practising the bragging.
I have told one guest already, so do not make me a liar.

quests.title: The third riddle
quests.text: The Old Man says the answer to his third riddle is a level 34 partner. He may be joking. Find out.

offer.name: Old Man
lines: My third riddle. What grows without eating and answers without a voice?
The answer, I have decided, is a partner at level 34. It is a poor riddle. Prove me right anyway.
Will you?
doneLines: A partner at 34. See? It grew and it answered. I told you the riddle was fine.
Here. Two of them, because a bad riddle deserves a good reward.
remindLines: Level 34. The riddle is bad and my answer is worse and I stand by both.
A riddle you can solve by walking is a good riddle for old legs.

You are not finished until level 36. You cannot be. I have decided.
Reach it and I will tell you what my real mat is like. Will you?
doneLines: 36. Good. My real mat is harder, faster and slightly worse for your knees. You are ready.
Here are proper shoes for a proper rival.
remindLines: Level 36. Not because I need it. Because you do and I am stubborn.
A rival who stops growing is just a person who used to be interesting.

You are not old enough to hear it, which really means your partner is not strong enough to carry it.
Level 38 and I will tell you. Will you grow a little for an old woman?
doneLines: Sit. Here is the story. It is about a person who sent everyone else to look at things so she would not have to.
Now you know me. Take this. It is lighter than the story.
remindLines: Level 38. Then the story. It is short and it is heavy.
I have waited years to tell it, so do not rush the last two levels.

Reach level 40 and the needle touches the end and finally means something.
Will you be my forty?
doneLines: FORTY. The needle hit the end and the little pin and stayed there. I have written it down twice.
Here. This is the best thing I own and I want it to be the best thing you have.
remindLines: Level 40. The needle is shaking just thinking about it.
I have cleaned the glass three times. The glass is clean.

Win one duel against anybody and I will accept that your cards exist.
One duel. Will you?

Here. Buy more cards. Do not tell anyone I said that.
remindLines: One duel, any duel. I am counting and I am being smug about it.
Cards, not luck. Well. Mostly cards.

Two duels. Will you?

There. That was worth two duels and a swim. Take this too.

Here. A prize from the sewers. It was not in the sewer. I brought it.
remindLines: Three duels. The pipe is dry. The smell is not. The cards are good.
I have shuffled them four times. They are as shuffled as they will ever be.

Here. A small reward for a small truth.
